title: Delayed dip changes show no robust rise after large flares in 48 selected TESS CPV stars
abstract: We test whether dip-pattern changes continue to increase after large flares in complex periodic variables (CPVs). We reuse released TESS change percentiles and compare paired windows before and after each flare. The windows omit the flare rotation and its neighbours. For 115 flares with equivalent duration at least 100 s in CPV sectors of 48 stars, the after-minus-before sharp-change percentile is -0.050 (95% star bootstrap interval -0.108 to -0.002). After exclusion of nearby large flares, it is -0.022 (-0.097 to 0.045; 78 events, 40 stars). Shorter windows give 0.017 (-0.057 to 0.084). On the same 82 events, one-day and half-day windows give -0.049 and 0.005. Thus no tested window gives a secure delayed rise, but a decline is not robust. The test does not give causal order within the flare rotation. It does not rule out a lasting step in the dip pattern, since such a step can leave later change rates unchanged. The primary paired sample retains 44% of central-eligible events. The source ranks, labels, masks and coverage limit the result. We provide a fixed design, code, aggregate results, hashes, a figure and an independent extraction check.

display.caption: Paired sharp-change percentiles before and after large flares. Panel A uses matched coverage within each lag pair; the event set changes across lags. Panel B omits the flare rotation and both neighbours. Bars are unadjusted 95% star bootstrap intervals. The shaded band is a descriptive margin of plus or minus 0.05 percentile units, not a physical exclusion limit.

citations.reason: Released event ranks and window code define the numerical input. We test delayed change asymmetry, beyond its central association test.
Reports flare-associated dip changes, with limited timing resolution.
Reports changes near flares and notes the unresolved causal order.
